selectedFeature.name: Bounded explicit project item evaluation with defaults, metadata and filesystem globs
selectedFeature.reason: One usable evaluation-only item pipeline closes the actual ItemGroup refusal across precedence, imports, item copies, ordered mutation and platform-sensitive globs. A parser-only ItemGroup addition would not meet the semantic objective.
selectedFeature.profile: Private SDK-less, namespace-free, controlled immutable fixture profile; ASCII identifiers and reached item data; Windows and Linux separately native-qualified; no public Microsoft.Build facade
selectedFeature.admission: Retain all existing property/import/condition restrictions except individually native-backed item-related transitions. Namespace, SDK resolver, implicit SDK imports and ambient environment remain excluded.
passes: Pass 1: validate/parse each reached project; preserve existing property/import evaluation and duplicate/cycle profiles. Record encountered ItemDefinitionGroup and ItemGroup sites with their real defining file and source coordinates in depth-first import order; do not evaluate their conditions or contents inline. Unimported files are not loaded.

Pass 2: after property/import evaluation completes, evaluate recorded ItemDefinitionGroup definitions in order against final properties and current per-item-type custom defaults. Definition-group conditions allow properties; definition/metadata conditions and values allow properties and current-type custom metadata. Item references and built-in metadata in definitions are explicitly outside this selected profile.

Pass 3: evaluate recorded ItemGroups and operations in order. Each operation reads an immutable snapshot of item state immediately before the operation, including self references. Publish its ordered result before the next operation. Final output retains surviving include-element order and multiplicity.

operations.Include: Expand properties once while leaving escapes intact; split raw semicolons with source trimming/empty-fragment rules; each fragment is a literal, a whole @(ItemType) reference, or an admitted glob. Preserve duplicates. Undefined/empty item lists contribute no items. Literal identities need not exist. Copy item references with metadata, then subtract operation-local Exclude and apply inline metadata.
operations.Exclude: Only on Include. Properties, semicolon lists, whole item references and selected patterns; references observe pre-operation state. Exclude removes only this Include's candidates, not earlier items. Same wildcard with different excludes must remain independent.
operations.Update: Select current items by literal/list/reference/glob matcher, without enumerating the filesystem; update every selected duplicate and no new items. Copy-on-write preserves already copied destination items and original include order/defining source. Inline metadata evaluates per selected item.
operations.Remove: Select current items using literal/list/reference/glob matcher, without enumerating the filesystem; remove all matched occurrences and preserve survivor order. No MatchOnMetadata in this profile.
operations.references: Whole @(Name) fragments and plain @(Name) expansion in admitted item/metadata scalar contexts. No transforms, functions, custom separators or mixed prefix/suffix item expressions. A property may contain a plain item-reference token: property pass leaves it unevaluated, item pass interprets it once at its proper expansion stage. Do not recursively reparse substituted property syntax.
operations.names: Case-insensitive ASCII lookup for item types/custom metadata, but preserve native-observed ItemType and metadata-name spelling in results. XML attribute/element structural names remain case-sensitive; do not reuse reserved-property key validation for metadata.

metadata.storage: Keep escaped identity and custom metadata until retrieval. Preserve distinction between absent and explicitly empty custom metadata. Source-derived effective metadata precedence: source direct metadata, accumulated inherited definitions, source item-type defaults, destination item-type defaults; new inline destination metadata overrides these. Preserve ordered default provenance until effective lookup, rather than flattening then accidentally overwriting source defaults.
metadata.references: Inline values/conditions support $(Property), @(ItemType), %(MetadataName) and %(CurrentItemType.MetadataName). Cross-item qualified metadata captures are refused; they are a separate Update batching semantic family. Evaluate each metadata child in declaration order; later siblings observe prior assignments. Built-in names cannot be assigned.
metadata.builtInRules: Identity is evaluated include; path-derived values use root project directory and source path rules, not current process working directory. RecursiveDir needs the original wildcard expression, and survives copied item references. DefiningProject* belongs to the Include that produced the destination item; Update retains original Include ownership. Request built-ins on demand; do not force invalid-path conversions for all literal identities. Native fixtures must fix exact strings, separators and copy behavior.
notSelected: public metadata Predecessor/Xml mutation and object identity
metadata.escapes: Item-specific scanner supports the ordinary reserved-character escapes %25 %2A %3F %40 %24 %28 %29 %3B %27, case-insensitive hex, decoded once after structural splitting. Escaped semicolon stays within one identity; escaped wildcard does not become a filesystem wildcard. Other percent escapes, control/non-ASCII item data and residual malformed expressions refuse in this profile. Do not globally widen the old property/import escape contract.

conditions.grammar: Reuse selected Boolean/equality/ordering/And/Or/Not/Exists/HasTrailingSlash syntax and bounds. Extend raw scalar reference recognition only at eligible item/metadata sites; condition expansion remains local to current properties/items/current metadata.
conditions.pathAndOwner: ItemGroup, item and metadata Exists paths use root project directory, even inside imports. Warning/error source owner and line remain the defining XML site. PropertyGroup/Import/ImportGroup paths retain their old defining-file rules.
conditions.cache: Keep immutable raw AST cache and exact-raw warning ownership behavior. Cache must never capture item lists, metadata tables, State, root or owner. Apply allowed-reference-kind validation at each site even on a cache hit; identical text accepted at an item site must not become accepted at a prohibited property/import site. Preserve >3000 eviction and existing group64/node256 limits.
conditions.falseSites: Static syntax/structure checks remain fail-closed for skipped sites; false item/group conditions skip expansion, glob traversal and metadata evaluation. This is a private adaptation wherever native skipped-input behavior differs.

globs.admitted: Relative slash patterns: * and ? within path segments; ** only as an entire path segment, including zero/multiple directory levels and **/x/** shapes. Literal fixed prefixes and ./ allowed; no rooted/drive/UNC/URI/backslash or parent-traversal patterns.
globs.enumeration: Enumerate only beneath the explicit root project directory within the declared sandbox. Distinguish filesystem enumeration from pure item identity matching used by Exclude/Update/Remove. Return file identities in native-observed representation and per-glob OrdinalIgnoreCase order, then preserve include-fragment/element order and duplicates. No global post-sort/deduplication.
globs.case: No universal Windows-fold/Linux-exact switch. FileMatcher.GetFilesForStep delegates simple patterns to platform enumeration, but DirectoryPattern shapes force per-file case-insensitive matching on Linux. Fixed-prefix directory lookup, wildcard directory lookup, recursive filename matching and exclusion matching need distinct captured expectations. Reject case-colliding sibling names in the private portable corpus/profile to avoid unqualified equal-key sorting order; ordinary mixed-case spelling remains covered.
globs.resourceAdaptation: Proposed private limits: at most 512 item/definition operations, 1024 live item occurrences, 64 metadata entries per item, 4096 visited filesystem entries per evaluation, traversal depth 32 and 64 path segments per pattern. Keep 16 project/import files and 65536 bytes per file. Limits are bounded-profile resource policy, not MSBuild limits; exercise limit and limit+1 controls, without expanding native parity totals.
globs.filesystemAdaptation: No symlink/junction/reparse traversal, including an apparently in-sandbox alias. Check every traversed directory and selected entry; refuse escapes and links, close DirectoryStreams on success/failure. Inputs are immutable fixtures, not a hostile concurrent filesystem security guarantee. No filesystem-result cache across evaluations. Source laziness/performance/read-set equivalence is not claimed for the eager bounded implementation.
globs.nativeCapture: Capture OS-specific results before implementation. Preserve actual * versus *.* behavior, ? behavior, missing directories and empty matches; do not replace native results with java.nio glob expectations.

outputAndExecution.model: Extend package-private Result with immutable ordered item snapshots and a case-insensitive type index, keeping existing property/import/diagnostic accessors and their types. Deep-copy lists/maps; later Update/evaluation or caller mutation cannot alter earlier snapshots. Store item operation/source provenance privately.
outputAndExecution.compatibility: Result is internal, not a substitute public EvaluationResult API. Preserve old six-argument construction if retained compiled consumers actually use it; inspect ABI before changing record components. Prefer additive accessors/helper immutable types over breaking old constructor descriptors.
outputAndExecution.noTaskExecution: Evaluation ends after selected passes. Targets remain inert under existing allowlist; DefaultTargets/InitialTargets never schedule work. Refuse UsingTask, task factories, SDK resolution, target-local ItemGroups, task outputs and execution requests. Native observer uses Project evaluation/GetItems only: no Build, restore or target switch.

outsideAndWhy: Full MSBuild and SDK-style projects, solution handling, Choose/When/Otherwise, import wildcards, toolset/environment/resolver prelude: independent deferred evaluation/configuration families; existing refusals remain.

Item transforms/functions/custom separators, mixed text/vector fragments, cross-item qualified Update metadata and MatchOnMetadata: distinct expansion/batching contracts; explicitly refused, not silently flattened.
Timestamp metadata, arbitrary Unicode/escapes, native exception/HResult/message ABI and hostile-filesystem race safety: not covered by the selected ASCII controlled-fixture profile.

Exact public Project/ProjectItem/ProjectMetadata facade, mutation/reevaluation/lifecycle identity, design-time ItemsIgnoringCondition/AllEvaluatedItems and paired .j workflow: open N01/Core representation work, not credited by internal snapshots.
Full cycle-chain diagnostics, complete platform matrix, full source reuse/release rights and distribution: remain acceptance gaps.

Extend existing MetadataLoadContext reader's selected scope to these exact anchors and directly consumed collection/string/bool/metadata identities, including visibility, accessor metadata, assembly/MVID/token and overloads; do not promote internal IItem/ItemSpec/FileMatcher to public contracts.

sourceFindings.finding: Definitions and items are separate passes after all properties/imports; group/item conditions use current lazy item state; ProcessItemElement receives root directory; definition expansion allows properties/custom metadata.
Root paths for item/metadata conditions; cloned updates preserve originating item element; ordered operation chains and intermediary item-reference capture; final items ordered by ElementOrder.
Property expansion precedes raw-semicolon split; item-expression fragments precede literal/glob classification; escaped wildcard handling differs from real glob; operation matcher is not enumeration.
Semicolon tokenizer trims and discards empty fragments; percent unescape must follow splitting.
Snapshot Exclude expansion; copies versus literals versus actual glob enumeration; source Include owns created destination; excludes occur before metadata.
Update clones selected items and applies per-item metadata; qualified cross-item metadata uses captured match state and cannot be guessed.
Remove matches current item identities; MatchOnMetadata is separate machinery.

Inline metadata values and conditions use per-item context, sequential sibling state, root condition directory; MaybeAdjustFilePath is platform-sensitive and must be checked on imported/path metadata fixtures.
Exact item/value/metadata API anchors; direct/built-in/default lookup; source direct/inherited/source-definition precedence over destination defaults; copy ownership differs from update ownership.
Pattern-shape-dependent Linux case semantics, not one global case rule.
Per-glob files sorted with StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase and reescaped before engine storage.
Pure glob matcher normalizes input/root and uses FileMatcher regex; does not imply filesystem enumeration behavior.
Exact built-in names; timestamps distinguished from stable path/defining-project metadata.

Non-source-only managed build enables Windows interop independent of host OS and uses runtime platform checks; presence of those compiled branches does not itself prove DLLs cannot run on Linux. Actual execution remains required.
